extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and library patrons interested in comics and graphic novels (including faculty and librarians)
extracted.subtask_description: A university library research guide summarizing the Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards (annual awards presented at San Diego Comic-Con), with emphasis on the Best Academic/Scholarly Work category and library holdings of nominated titles. Useful for locating award-winning or nominated scholarly books on comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eisner Awards — event and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards are given out each year at San Diego Comic-Con.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the awards are annual and presented at a major industry event (San Diego Comic-Con). No specific scoring rubric is provided on this page; the statement establishes timing and venue as part of the awards' context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose — creative achievement in the American comic book industry
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards are given for creative achievement in the American comic book industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses the overarching evaluative standard for Eisner Awards: recognition of 'creative achievement.' The page does not enumerate subcriteria (e.g., writing, art, innovation) or scoring weights, but implies winners are selected based on notable creative contributions to American comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Best Academic/Scholarly Work
rubrics_metrics.description: They also give out an award each year for best academic or scholarly work, many of which we have available in the Libraries in either print or digital format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies a distinct Eisner category recognizing scholarly publications about comics; the page lists the 2024 nominees (titles, authors, ISBNs, publication dates) as examples. It does not provide the nomination or selection criteria for this category, but it indicates the existence of a formal scholarly-work award and points users to a full list of previous nominees on Wikipedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library availability / access as a practical selection aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Many nominated works are available in the Libraries in either print or digital format. Individual entries include availability notes such as 'Available as an eBook' or call numbers for print copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not an evaluative criterion for the awards themselves, this provides practical guidance for researchers looking to consult nominated or winning works: check eBook availability or library stacks/call numbers. The page uses availability labels for each listed title (e.g., 'Available as an eBook', call number) and encourages consulting library holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: External reference for full nominee/winner lists
rubrics_metrics.description: You can see a full list of previous nominees in this category on Wikipedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide directs readers to external resources (Wikipedia) for comprehensive historical nominee and winner lists. This is procedural guidance for locating more complete award-history information beyond the brief examples on the page.
